extracted.intended_audience: implementers of MathML renderers and authors of MathML/XML math content (browser authors, tool/library writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative recommendations for serializing, validating, and rendering MathML (XML/HTML serialization, DTD/XSD usage, operator spacing dictionary, and element attributes). Targeted at implementers and authors producing or rendering MathML content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Namespace prefix usage in XML serialization
rubrics_metrics.description: it is recommended that namespace prefixes are not used in XML serialization of MathML to maintain compatibility with the HTML serialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the MathML DTD allows the use of namespace prefixes (via the Modularization strategy), avoid namespace prefixes in XML serialization to preserve compatibility with HTML serialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character entity references in XML serialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that unlike the HTML serialization, when using the XML serialization, character entity references such as ∫ may not be used unless a DTD is specified, either the full MathML DTD as described here or the set of HTML/MathML entity declarations as specified by [Entities].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer specifying characters directly or using numeric character references (e.g. ∫ or ∫) unless the appropriate DTD/entity declarations are present. If you need entity references, include the full MathML DTD or the HTML/MathML entity declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation using the MathML XML Schema
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML fragments can be validated using the XML Schema for MathML, located at http://www.w3.org/Math/XMLSchema/mathml4/mathml4.xsd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provided XSD was mechanically generated from the Relax NG schema and omits some constraints that cannot be enforced using XSD syntax — so XSD validation is useful but not complete; implementers should be aware some semantic/structural constraints are not checked by the XSD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator dictionary as normative default for operator spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The following table gives the suggested dictionary of rendering properties for operators, fences, separators, and accents in MathML, all of which are represented by mo elements. Note that implementations of [MathML-Core] will use these values as normative definitions of the default operator spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the operator dictionary entries as the default spacing semantics for mo elements unless overridden; treat these values as normative for MathML-Core implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator dictionary indexing by element content and form attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: The dictionary is indexed not just by the element content, but by the element content and form attribute value, together. Operators with more than one possible form have more than one entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining an operator's spacing/behaviour, consider both the operator glyph and its form attribute (prefix/infix/postfix/etc). The MathML specification also defines which form to use when no form attribute is given (see Default value of the form attribute).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator spacing units (lspace and rspace)
rubrics_metrics.description: The values for lspace and rspace given here range from 0 to 7 denoting multiples of 1/18 em matching the values used for namedspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret lspace/rspace as multiples of 1/18 em (0..7). Implementations should map these integer values to exact spacing amounts consistent with the namedspace convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-sensitive spacing for invisible operators (InvisibleTimes and ApplyFunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the invisible operators whose content is InvisibleTimes or ApplyFunction, it is suggested that MathML renderers choose spacing in a context-sensitive way (which is an exception to the static values given in the following table). For <mo>⁡</mo>, the total spacing (lspace + rspace) in expressions such as sin⁡x (where the right operand doesn't start with a fence) should be greater than zero; for <mo>⁢</mo>, the total spacing should be greater than zero when both operands (or the nearest tokens on either side, if on the baseline) are identifiers displayed in a non-slanted font (i.e., under the suggested rules, when both operands are multi-character identifiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not blindly apply static spacing values for these invisible operators — implement context rules: ensure ApplyFunction produces visible separation in function-application contexts (e.g. sin x) and InvisibleTimes produces separation when both operands are multi-character, non-slanted identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script-level spacing exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Some renderers may wish to use no spacing for most operators appearing in scripts (i.e. when scriptlevel is greater than 0; see 3.3.4 Style Change <mstyle>), as is the case in TeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At scriptlevel > 0 it is acceptable for renderers to reduce or eliminate operator spacing to mimic TeX behaviour; implementors may choose to override normal spacing in sub-/superscript contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator dictionary entry format and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first presentation, operators are ordered first by the form and spacing attributes, and then by priority. The characters are then listed, with additional data on remaining operator dictionary entries for that character given via a title attribute which will appear as a popup tooltip in suitable browsers. In the second presentation of the data, the rows of the table may be reordered in suitable browsers by clicking on a heading in the top row, to cause the table to be ordered by that column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator entries include form, priority, lspace, rspace and other properties. Provide machine-readable data (unicode.xml) and human-readable table views; support sortability for implementers and authors inspecting the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: groupalign / alignmentscope / side / minlabelspacing attributes (mstyle, mtable, mtr, mtd)
rubrics_metrics.description: mstyle.generalattributes, mtable.attributes, mtr.attributes, and mtd.attributes include attribute groupalign {group-alignment-list-list}?, attribute alignmentscope {list {('true' | 'false') +}}?; mtable.attributes also includes attribute side {"left" | "right" | "leftoverlap" | "rightoverlap"}?, attribute minlabelspacing {length-percentage}?. mtd.attributes has attribute groupalign {group-alignment-list}?. The group-alignment token set is "left" | "center" | "right" | "decimalpoint" and group-alignment-list-list is validated by the pattern '(... )*'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authoring MathML tables/rows/cells, use the groupalign and alignmentscope attributes with the specified value sets and list patterns. mtable supports side and minlabelspacing with the indicated types; mtd uses a single group-alignment-list. Follow the documented pattern for group-alignment-list-list when providing grouped alignment lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: mlabeledtr element structure and attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: mlabeledtr = element mlabeledtr {mlabeledtr.attributes, mtd+} and mlabeledtr.attributes = mtr.attributes. TableRowExpression |= mlabeledtr
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An mlabeledtr must contain one or more mtd children and may use the same attributes as mtr. Implementers/validators should accept mlabeledtr where table rows are labelled and apply the same attribute rules as for mtr.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of machine-readable operator data (unicode.xml)
rubrics_metrics.description: The data is all available in machine readable form in unicode.xml which is also the source of the HTML/MathML entity definitions and distributed with [Entities].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should use unicode.xml as the canonical machine-readable source for operator properties and entity definitions; authors/tools can reference or include this file for consistent behaviour.
